source.title: Data Whitening Improves Sparse Autoencoder Learning

record.tranche_reason: Evaluates sparse autoencoders on language-model activations, reporting benchmark results relevant to the claim's indirect-evidence version for real models; it does not reproduce the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own SAE benchmark results and a synthetic 2D sparse-coding simulation. The simulation has two sources and two dimensions, so it does not test overcomplete superposition. Prior claims about polysemantic neurons and SAEs are cited background, not results from this study. Reconstruction metrics are omitted from rows because they do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper uses SAEs as a tool and reports how its own preprocessing (PCA whitening) changes SAEBench scores, compared with unwhitened SAEs. It never measures whether LLM features are superposed, spread across neurons, or recovered by SAEs relative to a non-SAE baseline such as neurons. Its 2D simulation has two sources in two dimensions, so it has no superposition. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but overstated. The authors say whitening consistently improves interpretability metrics at a modest cost in reconstruction, and recommend it as a default preprocessing step. Their own Table 2, however, shows no significant SCR or TPP change for Top-K SAEs; only ReLU SAEs improve on all three metrics. They also argue that optimizing the sparsity–fidelity frontier alone does not guarantee interpretability.
record.recipe_differences: This study trains ReLU and Top-K SAEs on language-model activations with PCA whitening and evaluates SAEBench metrics; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects differ by SAE architecture: ReLU shows significant gains in all three reported interpretability metrics, while Top-K shows a significant sparse-probing gain but no significant SCR or TPP change.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA whitening of LLM activations significantly raises SAEBench sparse probing, SCR and TPP for ReLU SAEs. For Top-K SAEs it raises only sparse probing (SCR and TPP not significant). In both, reconstruction (CE loss score, explained variance) drops by about 2–5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whitening the SAE input improves SAE interpretability benchmark scores at a small cost in reconstruction, with an effect that depends on the SAE architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 2D sparse-coding simulation, whitening makes the landscape isotropic and aligns the sparsest solutions with accurate feature recovery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correlated, anisotropic inputs can misalign sparsity and feature recovery in sparse coding, and whitening realigns them.

record.problems: The LLM experiments cover two models at middle layers and below 2B parameters, and report aggregates across configurations rather than model-specific outcomes. The interpretability evidence is benchmark-based rather than direct validation against ground-truth features. The synthetic landscape is a 2D simulation; the paper notes that quantitative conditioning and gradient analysis on high-dimensional real activations remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: Reconstruction metrics (CE Loss Score and Explained Variance) are in Tables 1–2 but do not measure the claim versions. No other claim-relevant results were omitted.

untested.parts: All parts. There is no toy model with more features than dimensions, no sparsity transition, and no geometry analysis.
All parts. Capacity competition and polysemantic neurons are not measured.
All parts. Alternative causes of polysemanticity are not studied.
All parts. There is no comparison of SAE features against neurons or a baseline, and no measure of how features are distributed across neurons. Only whitened vs. unwhitened SAEs are compared.
All parts. Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not tested.
All parts. One-dimensional vs. multi-dimensional features are not compared.

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled this T3 and 'tests V4'. I reclassify it as T4: every LLM result is a whitened vs. unwhitened SAE comparison, which is the study's own method compared with the standard one. Superposition and polysemanticity appear only as cited background (Elhage et al. 2022). Leaving out the reconstruction rows was fine.

versions.untested_parts: No test of more sparse features than dimensions, overlapping directions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry.
No test of capacity pressure, polysemantic neurons, or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of whether polysemantic neurons arise through alternative mechanisms.
The SAE benchmark provides indirect interpretability measures, not direct evidence that particular ground-truth sparse features are recovered or spread across neurons.
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Synthetic 2D sparse-coding simulation
rows.operation_detail: Compared the simulated sparse-coding optimization landscape before and after PCA whitening.
rows.measure: Landscape geometry and alignment of sparsity with feature recovery
rows.baseline: Without whitening: narrow, elongated basin; high-sparsity regions can be misaligned with accurate feature recovery.
rows.value: With whitening: more isotropic landscape; high sparsity aligns with accurate feature recovery.
rows.note: This simulation uses two sources in two dimensions and therefore does not test superposition with more features than dimensions.
rows.check: A 2-source, 2-dimension sparse-coding landscape. It is not overcomplete, so it cannot show superposition. The result is qualitative and read from figures.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The SAE activations score positively on sparse probing and feature-disentanglement measures, with reported gains after whitening (r1–r3); these are indirect benchmark evidence, not direct ground-truth feature recovery.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Sparse probing improves (r4), but the reported SCR and TPP changes are not significant (r5–r6), so the interpretability measures do not improve uniformly across architectures.
